turns.prompt_text: I got a problem. I really like using SVGs. But there seems to be no free SVG Art Editors. GIMP is extraordinarily difficult to understand. I just want the very basic thing. I have an iPad mini and an apple pen, I wonder if there are any apps I could use that I could just use iCloud or Google Drive to move files that way.
turns.response_html:
Vector art on an iPad doesn't have to mean dealing with the desktop-style headache of GIMP or dropping a ton of money. Because you want something basic, intuitive for the Apple Pencil, and completely compatible with iCloud/Google Drive file swapping, there are a couple of excellent, free iPad apps to look into.

The top recommendations tailored specifically to a straightforward iPad workflow include:

1. Inkpad Libre

This is the absolute closest thing to a "hidden gem" for what you are trying to do. It is a completely free, open-source revival of a classic iPad vector app, and it purposefully collects zero data and features no hidden paywalls.

  • Why it fits: It has a completely streamlined, pared-down toolbar that handles basic shapes, paths, text, and layers without overwhelming you.
  • The Workflow: It integrates natively with the iPadOS Files app (iCloud Drive). You can open SVGs straight out of your drive, edit them with the pencil, and export them back as a clean SVG, PDF, or PNG.

2. Linearity Curve (Formerly Vectornator)

If you want something that feels a bit more modern and sleek but still completely leverages the Apple Pencil, this is an excellent choice.

  • Why it fits: While they have added premium tiers for heavy enterprise/marketing teams, their Free Plan is incredibly robust for individual creators. It features an intuitive "Auto-Trace" feature and standard path tools that feel completely natural with the Apple Pencil.
  • The Workflow: It fully supports standard iPadOS sharing. You can easily import SVGs from Google Drive or iCloud and use the standard "Export -> SVG" menu to save them right back to your cloud storage folders.

3. Assembly (By Pixite)

If the concept of plotting individual vector dots (bezier anchor points) feels tedious, Assembly takes a completely different approach.

  • Why it fits: It's a "building-block" vector editor. It gives you a massive library of basic shapes that you snap together, cut out, or merge to create crisp logos and illustrations. It’s highly visual and incredibly basic.
  • The Workflow: The basic version lets you build freely and export standard formats, though certain advanced shape packs require a subscription.

Recommended Workflow for Cloud Moving

To make moving files seamless between your cloud drive and these apps:

  1. Make sure you have the Google Drive or iCloud Drive app installed on your iPad mini.
  2. Open the default Apple Files app. On the left sidebar, ensure Google Drive is toggled "On."
  3. When using an app like Inkpad Libre, you can just select Import, browse straight into your Google Drive or iCloud folders, tap the SVG, edit it, and use Export to drop it right back into the exact same folder.

Which style sounds like a better fit for your projects: a classic pen-and-path layout like Inkpad, or a shape-snapping tool like Assembly?
